subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Quantum Computing Threats
description: Learn Quantum Computing Threats in one minute.

hook.text: Quantum computers could break the encryption protecting every bank, every government, and every website.

buildup.text: Current encryption relies on math problems that regular computers can't solve fast enough to crack.

discovery.text: NIST released post-quantum encryption standards in 2024. Migration will take years across global systems.

twist.text: Attackers steal encrypted data now to decrypt later when quantum arrives — called 'harvest now, decrypt later.'

climax.text: The quantum threat isn't just future risk. Stolen data today becomes exposed data tomorrow.

punchline.text: Steal encrypted data today. Crack it with quantum later.

quiz.question: What is 'harvest now, decrypt later'?
options: Stealing encrypted data now to decrypt when quantum arrives
Encrypting data twice for extra security
Harvesting computing power from idle machines
